1s4gx8a: The locomotive shed in Ingeniero White, built in 1907 and closed for almost thirty years, was reopened on Tuesday as a cultural centre. The opening exhibition, devoted to the port's railway workers, was presented by the mayor to some four hundred people, many of them children and grandchildren of those who worked in that workshop.
3yxvpq: The restoration was not quick. The roof was repaired in 2022 with provincial funds; the iron gates were taken down, cleaned and put back by a cooperative of local blacksmiths; and the pits where the engines were inspected were only partly covered, so that the public could see what they were like. According to the architect in charge of the works, Paula Rivas, every decision was discussed with the residents' association, which for years had looked after the building on its own.
1nz9m0z: During the ceremony, Rivas recalled that the first time she went into the building, in 2019, there was no electricity or water there and that roof let the rain in. «That day I thought it couldn't be saved», she admitted. 1a4uqj7: Visits are free. The winter opening hours will be announced at the end of the month; until then, the centre opens from Wednesday to Sunday, from 2 p.m. to 7 p.m. Anyone who has photos or documents from the workshop can take them to the entrance: they will be digitised and returned to their owners the same day.
